title: refactor(ui): unify shared controls, dialogs and links
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Standardizes text links, input styling, dropdown surfaces, tooltips, and icons in the shared UI package so apps use consistent controls.
- Makes dialog frames responsive and updates existing Enter and Economics dialogs to fit the available screen space. Dashboard forms and confirmations remain contained, with their existing footer buttons.
- Places section headings and actions inside their panels and removes duplicated spacing styles.
- Adds reusable confirmation dialogs, copyable fields, and key badges; updates the component showcase and accessibility tests.
- Validation: 80 UI tests pass, UI and Enter frontend builds pass, and UI/showcase/Playground/WebSim/Economics typechecks pass. Enter's standalone typecheck still reports an existing model-catalog `health.success_rate` mismatch. Browser appearance review is manual.

gist.headline: One garden, matching buttons
gist.blurb: The shared UI kit got its hedges trimmed: links, inputs, menus, tooltips, icons, and dialogs now grow from the same set of controls. Dialogs also learned the ancient art of fitting on smaller screens.
gist.summary: Standardized shared links, inputs, dropdowns, tooltips, icons, and panel spacing, while adding responsive dialog frames plus reusable confirmation dialogs, copyable fields, and key badges across Enter and related apps.
gist.impact: Users will encounter more consistent controls and screen-fitting account, API-key, endpoint, and Economics dialogs, while developers can reuse the new shared UI compositions with accessibility coverage.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy shared garden workbench represents the unified UI kit: matching buttons, link signs, dropdown pots, tooltip fireflies, copyable key badges, and a responsive dialog frame all fit together neatly. Polli acts as the observant gardener, adjusting a dialog window so it fits the little CRT monitor, with code-plants and small flowers showing that the same components are growing across several apps.
